How do I get an advance directive?
Almost all states require two witnesses (who usually cannot be relatives or healthcare providers) and/or a notary public to sign the document.

Where should I keep my advance directive?

Store your completed advance directive where a family member or legal representative can easily find it in an emergency. You could also store copies in a home safe.
Never keep your original advance directive in a bank's safe deposit box, as it would be difficult to access quickly. It's also a good idea to make copies of your advance directive and keep one in your car, in your wallet or purse and on your refrigerator (EMTs are trained to look there).
